metadata.datasource: Traced off the bitmaps of Kodak H-1-2302 (3-22), KODAK Black-and-White Print Film 2302 / 3302: its characteristic curve for D-97 at 21 C, 6.52 min, where the sheet's gamma-against-time plot reaches 2.5, the middle of the control gamma it develops to (2.4 to 2.6), interpolated between its 5 and 7 minute curves along exposure at each density (tungsten 1/50 s, diffuse visual). The sheet disagrees with itself: measured as it defines its control gamma (D-min + 0.95 to + 0.50 log E), its curves come out 0.23 to 0.47 above that plot at every time, this one 2.78, and its 5 minute curve (2.53) would meet the control gamma so measured; the plot's time is taken, the harder print of the two. The curves are plotted net of the base: base 0.048, the toe of the sheet's granularity plot (0.062, Status A green, 3 1/2 min) less its net fog at 3 1/2 minutes (0.014); D-min 0.065. Mid-grey (18.4% transmission) at log E 0, agx's rule for its print films. Spectral sensitivity at D-min + 0.2, 380-500 nm (blue-sensitive; nothing beyond), at the level that collects as much of agx's printer lamp (TH-KG3) as 2383 does through its filtration for Kodak Vision3 250D. Printing lamp TH-KG3 and projector K75P as agx's 2383. Its MTF and granularity are read, not modelled. One silver layer, carried as three identical channels.
